images.caption: Figure 1:Composition reduces every task’s reasoning by the same factor.When solved in isolation (top), each task receives more reasoning than it requires. When composed into a single prompt (bottom), the reasoning allocated to each task shrinks proportionally (yellow). Tasks with sufficient slack absorb this reduction and are still solved correctly, whereas the task that requires long reasoning falls below its requirement and thus fails.

Figure 23:Disattenuated Pearsonrrcorrelation of accuracy degradation across different conditions, i.e. model and composition size. Each pair of conditions (a cell in the heatmap) averages over datasets and, on the left, over models, on the right, over composition sizes.Left:The correlation is substantially larger when comparing accuracy degradation within the same model across different composition sizeskk.Right:By contrast, the correlation between different models is low, especially across model families, suggesting different architectures and training recipes lead to different tasks being fragile.
